thread.title: Midday Update: Earnings-Fueled Rally Stalls as Consumer Sector Suffers Miss

title: Midday Update: Earnings-Fueled Rally Stalls as Consumer Sector Suffers Miss
text:
Midday Update: Earnings-Fueled Rally Stalls as Consumer Sector Suffers Miss April 19, 2018, 12:59:37 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Weighed down by higher Treasury yields and the rising cost of commodities, Wall Street's major market averages drifted back into negative territory on Thursday with the Dow under pressure by losses in component stocks Apple ( AAPL ), Intel ( INTC ) and Proctor & Gamble ( PG ). 
The earnings-fueled rally on Wall Street suffered a setback Thursday when Proctor & Gamble and Philip Morris ( PM ) sent the consumer staple sector sharply lower while Apple and semiconductors were losing ground following a warning from Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) regarding slower smartphone sales. 
Losses were mitigated, however, by positive results from Dow component American Express (AXP), which beat profit and sales expectations. Alcoa (AA) topped EPS estimates on below-consensus revenue, and Novartis (NVS) reported better-than-expected results and reaffirmed their FY18 outlook. 
Besides quarterly misses, market participants shifted focus onto the 10-year Treasury note, which leaped past the 2.90% milestone, a threshold traders view as expensive to corporate borrowing needs. Economic data failed to curb the downtrade with jobless claims falling by just 1,000 to 232,000, close to expectations for a drop of 3,000. And although the Philadelphia Fed business outlook index was better-than-expected, some of its components pointed to brewing stagflation. Prices paid rose to a seven-year high while new orders fell. 
European markets were mostly lower in sympathy with Wall Street with miners and energy names limiting losses. Steel and aluminium prices spiked on sanctions against Russian metal manufacturers, while oil was gaining altitude for a third straight day following a Reuters report citing a Saudi official who expects oil futures to hit $100 a barrel. 
Crude oil was up $0.52 to $68.99 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.06 to $2.68 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $6.40 to $1,347.30 an ounce, while silver was up $0.01 to $17.25 an ounce. Copper was down $0.03 to $3.13 per pound. 
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was unchanged at $13.88 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 2.39% to $22.07. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 0.59% to 22.93 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.29% to $127.48. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.43% to $16.25.
